Program and Project Reporting 
 
 
 
INTRODUCTION 
 
The Combine Forum for this year is different from the last 33 years because it is the start of the new 
era for the Managalas Conservation Area and is now the second phase after Conservation Area 
(CA) declaration last November.  
The declaration is followed by the signing of an MOU between PWM and MCF during MCF’s 
planning meeting just few months back (September). The MOU clearly spells out roles and 
responsibilities of PWM and MCF.  
MCF will now take on more roles with the implementation of activities while PWM will only be 
here to facilitate. 
 
The Combine Forum is part of the Consensus Building Process where the process starts from the 
lowest Family unit, up to the clans, then onto the Zone levels and finally to the District Wide 
Forum. Issues discussed within the family units, clans and zones are then presented and discussed 
in the District Wide Forum.  
PWM and other stakeholders assist where they can in terms of providing guidance and available 
options so communities can decide and agree on the way forward. 
  
Hence, this Consensus Building Process/Rainforest Literacy Program has now evolved to 
Community Empowerment and Education Awareness with an objective to facilitate, mobilize and 
empower communities through traditional decision making processes and also inform, encourage 
community participation and networking in sustainable management and development and 
development options for the natural resource base. 
 
As stated above, this new approach has left out the other parts of this process and still maintaining 
the Scriptwriting workshop, Zone Forums and the Combine Forum. 
 
The Combine Forum was jointly implemented by Managalas Conservation Foundation (MCF) and 
Partners with Melanesians (PWM) and it was held in Yombu village, Zone 8 on October 29th – 
November 1st 2018. The participants from around the plateau were warmly welcomed by a sing sing 
group with the sound of the kundu drums and a variety of local fresh produce straight from their 
gardens. 
Despite logistical problems and other minor shortfalls during the 3 days forum, there was a good 
turn-out of people, plus we had two (2) very resourceful people from the Oro Provincial 
government representing Fisheries and Dept of Agriculture and Livestock.

District Wide Combine Forum. 
 
PURPOSE 
 
 
The purpose of the Combine Forum for this year as discussed above is basically for; 
- 
 the Managalas people to come together, discuss pressing issues brought forward from the 
Zone forums  
- 
Collectively identify the way forward for each of the issues. 
- 
Identify specific plans to bring forward in terms of sustainably managing the CA  
- 
Give the Managalas people are sense of direction and for further clarification regarding life 
after CA. 
- 
PWM and other stakeholders to guide the discussions, ensure the activity happened as 
planned and reports/acquittals are in place.   
 
DISCUSSION 
 
The Combine forum took place on 29th October – 1st November, 2018 at Joivi village, Zone eight 
(8). 
The three days’ forum saw a good number of turn out by both male and female from around the 
plateau. While there was no representation from Zone 10 presumably because of the distance to the 
Forum Venue and late confirmations of the Forum venues/dates, the issues discussed seem to fairly 
include them to some extent. There were two GoPNG reps at the provincial level; one from 
Fisheries and the other from Department of Agriculture and Livestock.  
To get a clear picture of the representation/participation, see the attendance list attached with the 
MCF Forum report.  
 
As per the Zone forums (x2) the seven (7) Issue were further discussed by representatives from 
each of the 11 Zones 
1. SLA activities in the Plateau 
2. Establishment of Afore Council of Women 
3. East CBO Petition 
4. Establishment of Council of Chiefs for Advisory role in LLG to pass law 
5. Establishment of Steering Committee    
6. Establishment of CA Committee  
 
Below is a summary of the actual discussions, focusing on the main points and leaving out the 
unrelated issues. 
*Note: Some discussion points are not listed in this report because they are administrative issues 
and PWM/MCF are to take note and deal with it separately.  
 
Issue # 1: ROLES & RESPONSIBILITIES OF PWM/MDF/CBO 
Discussion Points: 
- 
Basically under this issue, MCF Project Director Damien Ase took the lead respond by explaining 
the MOU signed between PWM and MCF in September. 
- 
This followed questions regarding the MOU: 
1. What is the difference between the MOU and the attached Sub-Contract? 
2. How long will the MOU be for? 

 
./3 
3. What is the purpose of the MOU? 
4. Why is this MOU not signed in the initial stage of this project? 
  
 
Even though, these are simple straight forward questions, this tells us that most people have just seen 
this MOU for the first time. 
 
Mr D. Ase went on to further explain the MOU so as to answer these questions highlighting the 
specified roles to be played by both parties 
 
A strong emphasis was made by the community that the MOU must be strictly followed by both 
PWM and MCF. 
Issue # 2: SLA activities on the Managalas Plateau 
Discussion Points: 
- 
PWM’s Program Manager, Rufus Mahuru went on to explain the SLA Program activities 
highlighting the budget for next year (2019) and further clarified the roles of PWM vs MCF/CBO 
under this program 
- 
MCF’s Project Director, Damien a DAL and Fisheries were given time to share specific experiences 
and they highlighted available options that the Managalas community can tap into within the Ijivitari 
district/Oro provincial government program/budget each year. Some of the areas highlighted are; 
 
DAL program areas:  
i. 
Export Tree/Crops 
ii. 
Livestock 
iii. 
Food security programs (highlighted specific small community projects) 
iv. 
Women in Agriculture (specifically for women) 
v. 
Flori-culture (specifically for women) 
 
 
Fisheries: the officer clearly highlighted that the Oro Provincial government/Ijivitari district 
have a lot of untapped resources that MCF can tap into. But first, MCF and CBOs NEED to 
get themselves organized. He specifically mentioned that he can assist any CBO/individual 
who is interested to do fish farming. 
 
 
NBPOL: Dr Darren Bito (entomologist) was also there sharing some experience and also 
highlighted the importance of CBOs getting themselves organized and to prioritize small 
projects that are suitable and will benefit their individual CBOs  
 
- 
The communities were then asked to discuss and prioritize top three (3) SLA activities. After a long 
discussion, they came up with the 3 activities and the budget given in percentage; 
 Coffee – 50% 
 Fresh Produce – 25% 
 Vanilla – 25% 
 
Issue # 3: East CBO Petition 
The petition was read by the CBO 
Manager for Zone 7A 
Response by D.Ase (the responses are partly 
done in English and the local dialect and 
therefore we can only capture what we heard) 
The 13 points; 
1. Misuse of funds by mostly West, 
previous and current management 
 
2. No fair representation for the bank 
account signatories 
 
3. No regular staff and board meetings 
 
4. Most MCF Staff not working and 
getting paid for nothing 
 
5. All Board and Management high office 
 
1. Unaware of the matter and will look into it 
 
2. Raymond Asip newly appointed signatory 
by MCF Board 
3. The meetings depend on PWM’s funding 
transfer schedule 
4. They are paid upon monthly submission of 
reports 
5. Usually no applicants from East when 
positions are advertised, they show no 
interest 

 
./4 
is dominated by West 
 
6. No transparency and accountability in 
current MCF office 
 
7. Current MCF/Board and Management 
to prepare and equipped to manage 
MCF 
 
8. 360 000 hectares is too much for 7 
MCF staff to work or cover due to 
distance and geographical difficulty 
 
9. Separate East/West office to allow and 
create jobs for people 
 
10. Women to be signatories to MCF Bank 
Account 
 
11. Women activities not effective 
 
12. West having too much ownership over 
current MCF office and no respect for 
the office 
 
13. Delay of opening of CBO bank 
accounts 
 
 
 
6. Will look into this administrative issue 
urgently. 
 
 
7. MCF office already set up and acquittal 
forms already in place. Financial structure in 
the process. 
 
 
8. Not enough money to employ more staff, 
admin costs alone eats up the budget 
 
 
9. It costs money to run an office, current staff 
is manageable 
 
10. Women not organized and therefore they 
need to start organizing themselves in the 
plateau 
 
11. PWM will employ a gender officer next year 
and that person will assist with Gender 
Empowerment activities 
 
12. Will talk to MCF staff and look into that 
matter 
 
13. CBOs to open up accounts themselves and 
does not necessarily need MCF to do it. 
MCF will only provide support letters  
 
Some responses were NOT captured because Mr D Ase was speaking in the local dialect 
 
After the reading of the Petition and the response, there was a long discussion, debate, and 
disagreement and it was done in the local dialect and we were unable to capture the details. 
 
However, the Petition was withdrawn by the Chief of Chief of Dareki village and the CBO Manager 
of Zone 7B.  
 
Mr D Ase was given the task of ensuring that points in the petition was dealt with in his capacity as 
the MCF Project Director. 
  
Issue #4: Gender Empowerment 
- 
Revive/Strengthen Afore council of Women 
A bit of information was given (verbally) to enlighten the minds of the women who were present during the 
forum, with emphasis on further need for awareness/information dissemination throughout the plateau and to 
organize themselves at the CBO level up 
  
Way forward as discussed; 
- 
PWM to employ a Gender Officer to guide/coordinate with MCF Gender Officer to 
mobilize women in the plateau to set up this office come January 2019 
- 
Ensure the steps and process followed to setting up the Afore Council of Women are done in 
line with the Provincial/National Council of Women and the by-laws of PNG. 
 This is what the government should do but NGO is now taking the lead to facilitate 
and therefore, the Oro Provincial Council of Women executives must be notified and 
let them play their part. 
 PWM and MCF to work together with the Provincial and Local Level Government 

 
./5 
to ensure the Afore Council of Women is set up. 
 
 
Issue # 5: Establishment of Council of Chiefs for advisory role in LLG to pass law 
MCF Project Director only provided information on this issue, highlighting its importance and benefit. 
 
Way forward as discussed; 
- 
This forum agreed that it is important that they have the CoC set up and make it a part of the Afore 
LLG. 
- 
It has to be registered as a legal entity. 
 
Issue # 6: Establishment of Steering Committee 
Information was given by Mr D.Ase to be deliberated at a different avenue when there is a clear and better 
understanding of issues between the parties involved. 
 
Issue # 7: Establishment of CA Committee 
- 
Mr Patrick Vuet from Parttners with Melanesians explained; 
 
what CA is all about? 
 
Role/functions of CA Committee 
 
Composition of CA Committee members 
 
Set up of Rangers 
 
Reporting processes 
 
CA Management Plan  
 
- 
Mr D Ase also, explained further in-response to few questions raised in regards to the establishment 
of the CA Committee. 
 
- 
The forum then revisited the people appointed (x7) during the East/West Zone forums. There was a 
long discussion and debate especially with the term “landowner” and eventually only 4 people were 
appointed through a consensus. The four  (4) people are; 
West; 
 
Eta-Mary (Female rep) 
 
Standford Arore (Male rep) 
East; 
 
Ethel Avejari (Female rep) 
 
Andrew Bakai (Male rep) 
 
Way forward as discussed; 
- 
The names of the 4 appointed people above will be sent to CEPA for further deliberations on the 
processes and setting up of the full CA Committee. The appointees will then follow necessary 
processes to take office as according to CEPA. 
 
 
 
RESULTS/FINDINGS 
 
As per my observation; 
1. The logistics on ground was not as expected, participants were accommodated outside of the 
forum area. It was raining in the mornings and participants had to take shelter until the rain 
stops. They were late for the morning sessions. Access to river/creek was a problem to 
participants because it was distance away from where they were accommodated. 
2. The Forum Process was not followed resulting in discussions going off track/diverted from the 
main issues of concern.  

 
./6 
3. Network/link was created with the Provincial Fisheries and DAL office and this is an 
opportunity for the CBOs to make use of this opportunity especially with SLA activities in their 
respective CBOs. 
4. The roles and responsibilities of MCF/PWM have now been spelt out clearly during this forum 
with reference to the MOU signed recently which means this year in, year out issue on “ROLES 
and RESPONSIBILITIES” will no longer be an issue. 
5. During the combine forum a lot of issues were not discussed in depth because they were not 
clearly understood. This showed that CBO’s on the ground are not creating enough awareness in 
their respective zones regarding the issues. 
6. When organizing such forums in the near future, first and foremost, we must always look at 
accessibility to clean and safe drinking water and road. A lot of participants walked a distance to 
access the above which resulted in their late attendance at the forum. 
7. More networking must be established between responsible authorities of the government so that 
they can also have their say in the sustainable management of the plateau by working alongside 
with MCF/CBO’s in the CA. 
 
 
 
 
CONCLUSION 
 
The Combine Forum is a great avenue for the people of Managalas to come together come end of 
each year to discuss and identify way forward for the benefit of all. Hence this avenue must be 
maintained and taken seriously if the Managalas people want progress and development in the 
Plateau. 
 
RECOMMENDATION 
   
 
My recommendations are on areas that I feel strongly towards as per my working experiences in 
local communities including the Managalas Plateau. 
 
1. Community Empowerment and Education Awareness Program 
This program is vital and its activities must be revisited/redesigned and aligned with its 
Purpose/objective since it has shifted away from Rainforest Literacy and a part of the 
consensus building process left out. Theatre activities must be included because it is the 
only medium currently being used for awareness and information dissemination purposes 
around the plateau.  
Also, this scriptwriting workshop be changed to content development workshop or 
something along that line (only a suggestion) because as it is, we are no longer developing 
radio scripts for the radio programs and learning objectives for the print materials like it 
used to be. 
The lessons learnt from this Program especially in Managalas must be taken into careful 
consideration and NOT repeated in the new Project areas. 
 
2. Also have a Neutral Forum Facilitator 
It is always essential to have a facilitator who is neutral and will not take sides. Having a 
fair and balanced discussion is fundamental for an effective consensus building process. 
Therefore, facilitation of any forum in the near future must always have a neutral facilitator 
and also a co-facilitator to take on the facilitators responsibility if need be. 
 
3. There is a Need to Identify Proper Program Activities    
In addition to recommendation #1, there is a need to revisit the Consensus Building 
Process/Rainforest Literacy and clarify certain changes. We should be careful NOT to 

 
./7 
repeat the Managalas experience in other project areas because obviously their social 
structure and fabric of society is completely different. Therefore, we must seriously look at 
how best the overall program will suit individual areas.

MEDIA INVITE

Monday 08'" of September, 2018
ATTENTION: News Editors
Dear Sir/Madam,

Partners With Melanesians (PWM) Inc kindly request your esteemed organization to assign a
Journalist/Reporter to attend the Annual District Wide Combine Forum that will be held at Koeno
Village, Zone 6 in Afore LLG, Oro Province from October 29" — 01 November.

The District Wide Combine Forum will include local representatives of the 152 clans, from the East
and West area of the Managalas Plateau, PWM staff, invited guests and dignitaries. The way forward
for the locals and important issues which affect the people of the Managalas Plateau will be discussed
at the District Wide Combine Forum, this is the first District Wide Combine Forum after the
Managalas Plateau was declared as a Conservation Area on the 29" of November, 2017.

PWM will be responsible for return air tickets, local transport (by road), accommodation, meals and
communication during the District Wide Combine Forum.
Only provide Per Diem to your Journalist/Reporter per your normal organizational rate.

e Return to Port Moresby: November 2", 2018

Please confirm the attendance of a Journalist/Reporter by 4:00pm Thursday 11" of October.

To RSVP and for further information, contact Community Empowerment and Education Awareness
Coofdinator Veronica Aure on 7325 9746 or 323 6344.

ENN MONDIAI
Executive Director/ SFO

 “Maintaining the Dance” 
 
Program and Project Reporting 
 
 
 
INTRODUCTION 
 
The Managals Zone Forums are an annual activity that happens right before the Combined Forum 
and it involves the participation of Partners with Melanesians/Managalas Conservation 
Forum/CBOs and the local communities of Managalas Conservation Area. 
Initially, the zone forums are an avenue for the communities to come together, discuss issues and 
reach a consensus. So the Consensus process starts from the lowest Family unit, up to the clans, 
then onto the Zone levels and finally to the District Wide Forum where they present their issues and 
PWM try to look at suitable/available options to assist them find answers. 
PWM either bring in specialist/partners through capacity building trainings/workshops. Also, 
through the Rainforest Literacy Program, it tries to inform/educate and/or create awareness using 
the multi-channel system where a number of different mediums are used depending on the needs of 
the audience. 
 
For this year the Zone Forums (X2) is seen as Phase two (2) after the CA declaration last year and it 
has changed its focus giving more emphasis on community empowerment and still maintaining its 
education/awareness component. The men, women and children should now be empowered to take 
full ownership and be self-reliant as custodians of the Managalas Conservation Area. They should 
be able to identify solutions to their issues/problems, do what they can in their capacity and PWM 
will only come into facilitate. 
  
People came from around the plateau to the two selected venues (Dareki Village – East) and 
(Tahama village – West) and spend about a week each to discuss issues and identify the way 
forward. 
The Zone Forums are jointly implemented by Managalas Conservation Foundation (MCF) and 
Partners with Melanesians (PWM). 
MCF Literacy Field Coordinator, Crispine Burawa took the lead in both of these forums, while 
PWM assisted where we are being asked to.    
 
PURPOSE 
 
 
The purpose of the Zone Forums for this year as discussed in the introduction above is basically; 
- 
for the people from the Eastern side and the Western side of the plateau to come together 
and discuss pressing issues that arise in the course of the year 
- 
identify the way forward for each of the issues 
Project name 
Managalas Conservation Foumdation (MCF) 
Program name 
Community Empowerment & Education Awareness 
Program activity 
Zone Forums (East & West) 
Reporting period 
27th September – 9th October 2018 

 
./2 
- 
PWM to guide the discussions, ensure the activity happened as planned and 
reports/acquittals are in place   
 
DISCUSSION: ZONE FORUMS (EAST & WEST) 
 
The East Zone forum took place on 1st – 3rd October, 2018 at Dareki village, Zone 7A while the 
West Zone Forum took place on the 5th – 7th October, 2018 at Tahama village, Zone 2.  
The two and a half days’ forum from both sides saw a good number of turn out by both male and 
female from majority of the Zones/Wards. While there was no representation from Zone 9, Zone 4 
and Zone 10 presumably because of the distance to the Forum Venue and late confirmations of the 
Forum venues/dates, the issues discussed seem to fairly include them to some extent.  
To get a clear picture of the representation/participation, see the attendance list attached with the 
MCF Forum report.  
 
A total of eight (8) pressing issues came out of the Scriptwriting Workshop held earlier on in the 
year and this followed theoretically by the information dissemination/education awareness through 
the Managalas Theatre Group led by Alking.Fufus.  
The 8 issues are; 
1. Roles and Responsibilities of PWM/MDF/CBO on the plateau 
2. SLA activities in the Plateau 
3. Establishment of Afore Council of Women 
4. East CBO Petition 
5. Establishment of Council of Chiefs for Advisory role in LLG to pass law 
6. Establishment of Steering Committee    
7. Establishment of CA Committee  
8. Gender Empowerment 
 
Out of these 8 Issues, the Issue on Roles and Responsibilities was given to the Theater Group to 
create awareness and inform communities around the plateau. According to reports and as evident 
during the Forum, they have done their part well.  
The other 7 issues were given to the respective CBO’s to carry out awareness and for general 
information dissemination purposes to prepare the communities to participate constructively in 
these Zone Forums (x2) 
 
Thus, below is a summary of the actual discussions for both forums, focusing on the main points 
and leaving out the unrelated issues. 
The only issue not shared by both (East/West) is the ‘East CBO Petition’ which will be discussed 
by both sides during the Combine Forum. 
*Note: Some discussion points are not listed in this report because they are administrative issues 
and PWM/MCF are notified and will deal with it separately.  
 
Issue # 1: ROLES & RESPONSIBILITIES OF PWM/MDF/CBO 
Discussion Points 
- 
PWM is seen as playing the role of/by passing CBOs/MCF in-terms of activity implementation 
leaving CBOs/MCFs with nothing to do 
(Point raised by both E/W but a stronger emphasis came out by West with the intent that PWM 
should leave Managalas) 
- 
PWM management seem to override MCF Board’s decisions 
(Point raised by the East) 
- 
There should be a good  working relationship between PWM and MCF/CBOs (Point raised by E/W) 
- 
MCF to accompany Theater Group when they are doing awareness/disseminating information to 
further clarify on certain issues (Point raised by East) 
- 
Clear flow of channel of Communication from PWM to MCF/CBOs and eventually down to the 

 
./3 
communities in terms of implementation and reporting/acquittals (Point raised by the West) 
 
Issue # 2: SLA activities on the Managalas Plateau 
- 
A number of SLA activities have been identified apart from Coffee which is listed as the main 
activity  
For a details of specified activities, refer to MCF report by C.Burawa/A.Fufus  
(Point raised by both East/West) 
- 
PWM/MCF has misused previous SLA funds  (Points raised by both East/West) 
- 
Apart from the so many income generating options that we can engage in, we chose conservation so 
how does PWM/MCF come in to fully support CBOs under the SLA program funding  
(Points raised by West) 
- 
PWM to do a rapid survey/assessment through-out the Plateau on potential SLA activities and bring 
in partners/experts to assist us (Point raised by West) 
- 
Funding for SLA activities for next year (2019) must be given to the CBOs while MCF/PWM to 
only give advice/support and monitor the activities  and ensure reporting/acquittals are on time and 
up to standard (points raised by both East and West with a lot of emphasis on previous/current 
experiences of funds misuses) 
- 
PWM to link/create partnership between MCF/CBO and businesses/banks for loans etc (Points 
raised byWest) 
 
 Issue # 3: East CBO Petition 
Discussion Points 
Way forward 
- 
MCF/CBOs not fully equipped to take 
on the role as yet 
- 
No financial system in place 
- 
MCF has no other funding sources 
- 
MCF lack the capacity to fund raise and 
network  
- 
MCF Board dominated by the West 
- 
MCF senior positions dominated by the 
West 
- 
Signatory to the MCF are all from the 
West 
- 
CBOs has no office on Plateau and 
that’s why funds for activities are miss 
used 
 
- 
PWM to remain on Managals Plateau to continue 
build up their capacity, assist to set up their 
financial system 
- 
MCF to work closely with PWM and over time, 
PWM will eventually transfer the full 
responsibility and roles to MCF 
- 
Revisit appointment of MCF Board members and 
ensure there is fair represented from both East 
and West 
- 
Change all signatories  
- 
ALL MCF positions to be re-advertised including 
the Project Director  
- 
CBOs to set up office on an agreed central 
location, so discussions of any activity to be 
implemented on ground are discussed in the 
office with the presence  responsible Program 
Coordinators from PWM/MCF and the CBOs  
Issue #4: Gender Empowerment 
- 
Revive Afore council of Women 
This was the only activity/issue that was discussed under the main issue of Gender Empowerment and the 
discussion was particularly led by MCF Gender Officer. It was obvious, the participants had no clear 
understanding about the role and benefit of reviving the Afore Council of Women and therefore participants 
had very little input during both forums. 
However a number of women were selected as candidates for the chair lady position/members and as 
announced, women through-out the plateau were encouraged to attend the Combine Forum which will be 
held on 29th October – 1st November 2018 
 
Way forward as discussed; 
- 
MCF/PWM to guide/assist MCF Gender Officer to fully understand the Role of the Afore Council of 
Women and how it will benefit NOT only the WOMEN but MEN of the Managalas Plateau 
 
- 
MCF Gender Officer to mobilize Gender Reps from each CBOs, women/mother’s Groups registered 
under IPA, Church Fellowship Groups etc      
 

 
./4 
 
Issue # 5: Establishment of Council of Chiefs for advisory role in LLG to pass law 
Both The East and West side had very little to no constructive contribution to this issue. 
 
Way forward as discussed; 
- 
Participants were asked to let their respective chiefs know that they have to attend the Combine 
Forum to elect their council of Chiefs 
Issue # 6: Establishment of Steering Committee 
Lead Facilitator ruled this issue out as it was a management Issue 
 
Way forward as discussed; 
Lead Facilitator asked CBOs to deal with this issue 
 
Issue # 7: Establishment of CA Committee 
For this issue, only a handful of participants gave constructive ideas/views while the rest indicated that they 
need more information on the Role of the CA Committee and all other necessary information on establishing 
a CA in general. But despite that they eventually appoint 2 males and 2 females on the East side. 
While the West appointed 2 males and 1 female. 
 
Way forward as discussed; 
- 
The 7 appointed people (named) will go into an election during the upcoming Combine Forum and 
only 4 out of the 7 will form the CA Committee. To ensure there is fair representation in the 
Committee, there will be a male and a female from the East and a male and a female from the West. 
- 
A representative from SEPA should be present during the Forum to explain what the CA Committee 
is all about and its role 
As mentioned, a lot of discussion was spent on issue number 1 and the discussion went out of hand. 
PWM/MCF management are now aware of it and should be able to respond according if these issues arise 
during the Combine Forum.  
 
RESULTS/FINDINGS 
 
As per my observation; 
1. The Community Empowerment & Education Awareness Program formally Consensus Building 
/Rainforest Literacy Program to be clarified to the community whether it has totally changed its 
focus from Education/awareness and information dissemination to community empowerment, 
and how does Community Empowerment comes into play in this program. The participants were 
asking from time to time during both East and West Forums 
2. Forum process must be strictly followed in-order to avoid discussions to go off track where in 
most cases sensitive issues which are not part of the forum issues will arise   
3. Administrative issues should be identified and left out of the forum discussion because 
discussions go out of hand when it comes to sensitive administrative issues that are supposed to 
be solved at the administrative level, unless it requires members of the community to discuss 
during the forum 
4. It is obvious that most issues given back to CBOs to discuss with their respective community 
members are not done. And therefore participants were unable to contribute constructive views 
on these issues during the forum. But on the other hand, were the CBOs well equipped with the 
information they needed and whether they understood what they were supposed to do is the 
question 
5. Lead Facilitator/assistant facilitators must have at least background information on any technical 
concepts that are linked to the issues identified for discussions. Better still, PWM officers should 
be present during Zone Forums if the issue involves their program activities. Otherwise, the 
facilitators did ok for both this forums.  
6. The Venues of the next Zone Forums (East/West) should be decided and agreed at the end of 
both forums and forum dates to be communicated to all Zones a week or two in advance.   

 
./5 
7.  There was no gender activities happening this year even though MCF has a Gender Officer. 
This is evident during the forum when it comes to discussing the issue on Gender 
Empowerment. 
8. The logistics of the forum was well organized by the respective CBOs    
 
CONCLUSION 
 
By way of conclusion, this program more or less is the core of all other programs and requires all 
program officers from both MCF/CBO and PWM to assist as and when needed especially when it 
comes to providing and clarifying technical/other information. 
Hence, when program officers strictly follow the roles and responsibility guideline, PWM/MCF 
will have less problems/issues to deal with and focus more on achieving program goals.   
 
RECOMMENDATION 
   
 
My recommendations are on the two areas that I feel strongly towards as per my working 
experiences in local communities including the Managalas Plateau.  
1. Information dissemination and Education Awareness 
For any project/initiatives, information dissemination and education awareness is vital and it 
is an on-going activity and therefore this program (Community Empowerment & Education 
Awareness) is vital. As such, I would like to recommend that MCF/PWM management look 
into further developing the Managalas Theatre Group in terms of follow-up trainings for the 
theatre members because this is the only medium currently used in the plateau. They seem 
to be doing a great job as far as this program activity is concerned.  
Also, apart from follow-up trainings they should be equipped with simple materials that 
would enhance them to drive the key messages through. 
 
2. Gender 
Women are the core of development in all societies and their efforts are in most cases not 
recognized because of a number of reasons depending on cultural settings.  
Having said that, women are now beginning to be vocal about their participation in any 
developmental process and MCF already has a Gender Officer in place and there are Gender 
Representatives in each of the CBOs.  
So MCF with guidance from PWM, should look into avenues on how to mobilise the 
women and girls of Managalas to fully participate and have a voice in this 2nd phase, now 
that Managalas is a Conservation Area.

COMBINE FORUM-UGUNOMO VILLAGE-ZONE 5  
 
 
 
 
 
16-20 December, 2013 
 
FORUM REPORT) 
 
 
Prepared for Partners with Melanesians Inc. (PwM) 
Prepared by  
ENVIRONMENTAL LEGAL SERVICES (ELS)

1   
INTRODUCTION 
The submission for declaration of the Managalas Plateau as a Conservation Area (The Act) under the 
Conservation Areas Act was submitted by community representatives from the plateau with the support by 
Partners with Melanesians (PwM) to the Minister for Environment & Conservation Hon. John Pundari in the 
presence of Oro  Governor, Hon. Gary Juffa and Member for Sohe. Thereafter as required under the Act 
advertised in the newspaper in early 2013. The 90 day period for objection lapsed lapsed on 18 May 2013.  
An objection letter dated  18 March, 2013 was sent to the Minister for Environment & Conservation by the 
President of Afore Local Level Government, Hon. Douglas Garawa MPA on behalf of the landowners in the 18 
wards of the Afore LLG. The Department has not responded to the objection letter by the President of Afore 
Local Level Government to the Minister for Environment & Conservation although a draft response letter was 
prepared during the year. No satisfactory reasons have been provided by the Department for the long delay in 
responding to the objection letter. One year has lapsed after the submission for declaration of the 
Conservation Area was given to the Minister for Environment & Conservation on 8 November, 2012. As a 
result the President of Afore LLG has stopped al project activities on the plateau until he receives the 
response from the Department. This has affected properly planning and funding arrangement for project 
activities especially activities leading up to the official declaration of the Conservation Area after its approval 
by the National Executive Council and declaration by the Governor General and subsequent gazettal as 
required under the Conservation Areas Act. 
 
In May 2013 I was engaged by PwM to hold was to hold consultative meetings in selected places with 
stakeholders to verify the support for the objection to the declaration of the Managalas Conservation Area  by 
the Afore LLG President. The trip was from 23 May-2nd June 20013 and a report was furnished to PwM with 
eleven (11) recommendations to enable the stakeholders especially PwM to address the issues raised in the 
objection letter by the Afore Local Level Government President. Since then numerous correspondences have 
been exchanged between PwM, MDF and the President of ALLG with regard to the issues raised in the 
objection letter with a view to resolving them so that the declaration of the Conservation Area can proceed 
after the NEC approves its declaration  as required under the Conservation Areas Act but no agreement was 
reached by the parties thus the need for a plateau/LLG wide Forum to discuss the issues raised by the 
President in his objection with a view to resolving them. PwM decided that it was better for people from the 
area who have the standing and respect from the community and who are well versed with the projects 
objectives and programmes to facilitate at the Forum and guide the stakeholders to discuss and address the 
issues raised in by the President of ALLG  in his the objection letter to the Minister for Environment & 
Conservation. This was main reason PwM engaged myself to facilitate at the forum with assistance from 
Simon  Savaiko, a member of the Board PwM. The forum was held at Ugunomo village from 16-20 December 
2013. The forum was well attended by clan elders from all cultural zones on the plateau and community 
leaders wherein they discussed the five (5) issues selected by the Facilitators in consultation with PwM and 
through that addressed the issues raised by the President in his objection letter to the Minister. 

3 
 
 
2. BACKGROUND   
 
“ A PEACEFUL AND SELF RELIANT COMMUNUAL SOCIETY LIVING IN HARMONY WITH NATURE” 
This is the vision of Managalas people through their duly constitution entity , the Managalas  Development 
Foundation (MDF). 
 
The Managalas plateau in Oro Province of Papua New Guinea harbours a diverse array of fauna and flora. And 
more significantly the plateau is home to the Queen Alexendra Birdwing Butterfly, the world’s  largest 
birdwing butterfly  which is listed on Appendix 1 of the CITES Convention and which is only endemic to Oro 
Province of Papua New Guinea. The proposed Managalas Conservation Area covers 360,000 hectares of 
pristine rainforest comprising lowland mountane forests and is also the water catchment area of the Popondetta 
plains. The total population of the area is 18,000 under the Afore Local Level Government of the Ijivitari 
District. The people live in 75 villages made up of 152 sub-clans with ten (10) tribal groupings and speak four 
(4) dialects.  
 
The people on the Managalas Plateau are well aware of the impacts of large scale environmentally destructive 
projects like logging, mining and oil palm plantations. Having being working with international and national 
NGO partners since the early 1990’s the area is now  in the process of being designated as a conservation area 
under the Conservation Areas Act of 1978. The Managalas people  submitted the Managalas Proposed 
Conservation Area Application to the Minister for Environment and Conservation on 8th of November, 2012. 
As required under the Act, the  public advertisement was placed in the newspapers (Post Courier) for  
stakeholders to view and file any objections if any. The advertisement appeared in the Post Courier on 18 
February, March 4, March 18, April 1, April 29 and finally May 13 2013. The 90 day period expired on 18 
May 2013. The President of Afore Local Level Government, Douglas Garawa filed an objection in a letter 
dated 18 March 2013 wherein he raised a lot of issues why the  Minister should not make the NEC submission 
for it to approve the CA declaration and for the proposal to be shelved until such time the Managalas people are 
able to manage the project themselves. The Department to date has not officially responded to the objection 
letter by the President of Afore LLG and no reasons have been given for this long delay in responding to the 
objection letter and no reasons have been given by the Department for this long delay in responding to the 
President’s objection letter..  
In May 2013 PwM carried out its own independent consultation to verify the support by the clan elders for the 
objection filed by the President of Afore LLG engaging myself for this purpose. The consultation was 
undetaken out and a report was furnished to PwM which among others recommended for all project activities 
on the plateau to be put on hold until the issues raised in the objection letter by the President are addressed and 
resolved. It was found that  that majority of the clan elders on the plateau did not sign the objection letter by the 
President. Thereafter, PwM has been communicating with the President to try and hold  meetings to resolve the 

4 
 
issues he has raised in his objection letter but the President refused to attend such meetings saying he will need 
to get an official response from DEC on his objection letter first. The President also stopped all project 
activities saying he still stands by his objection. This affected the implementation of project activities by PwM 
and its local partner Managalas Development Foundation (MDF).  
 
3.   
Keys Issues Discussed at the Forum 
There were four main issues which were discussed at the forum. These issues were selected based on the 
concerns and issues raised by the President of Afore Local Level Government in his objection letter to the 
Minister for Environment & Conservation dated 18 March 2013 when the submission was made by PwM and 
MDF to the Minister to have the Managalas Plateau declared a Conservation Area under the Conservation 
Areas Act on 8 November 2012. These four issues which was agreed to by the Facilitators and PwM 
management are  as follows: 
Issue # 1. Future of the Proposed Managalas Conservation Area 
 
“The Managalas people will not be pushed around and forced to accept this conservation 
agenda by adamant, manipulative and self centered individuals using the NGO movement 
to further their hidden agendas  and secure employment for themselves in the name of 
conservation”. 
 
The above statement was made by the President of Afore Local Level Government (ALLG) in his objection 
letter to the Minister for Environment and Conservation. 
This issue was the main issue which needed to be discussed and resolve at the Forum especially in light of the 
objection by the President of Afore Local Level Government to the submission made to Minister for 
Environment & Conservation for declaration of the area as conservation area under the Conservation Areas 
Act. If this issue was not resolved then there was no need to proceed to the other issues which were 
specifically chosen to strengthen the work to have the area declared a conservation area which is the main 
objective of the Managalas Conservation Area Support Project (MCASP). Therefore considerable amount of 
time was consideration amount of time was spent on discussing this issue at the forum. The question we 
posed for the forum was “do we all agree to have the plateau fenced so we can keep outsiders out from 
intruding onto our lands or do we leave it open for outside intrusion”?  This question triggered a lot of 
discussions on the issue around the reasons for the initiative, what went wrong along the way and how we 
can collectively resolve the issues especially those raised by the President in his objection letter to the 
Minister. There were still confusion between conservation and land registration so many questions were 
asked on this issue although we know that this was issue of discussions in the early years leading up to the 
submission to the Minister. However, it did go to show that there is need for on-going awareness and public 

5 
 
education on such important issues as a lot of young people are now getting educated and so begin to get 
involved in issues at the community level and are curious about such issues because of what they read or hear 
through the media or through other mediums of communication. It was also brought to light that the 
influence of churches particularly the new charismatic movement on such issues raised confusions in the 
minds of people especially the younger generation who were not involved in the initial stages of the project. 
 
Issue #  2. 
 Relationship, Collaboration and Partnership between Partners with  
 
 
Melanesians (PwM), Managalas Development Foundation (MDF) and  
 
 
the Community Based Organisations (CBOs)  
 
This issues was selected as a discussion issue at the forum not only because of the issues and concerns raised 
by President of Afore LLG in his objection letter regarding management of the project by outsiders but also 
because of the important role that MDF and the CBOs play in implementing project activities under the 
MCASP and in light to PwMs plans to relinquish management responsibilities to MDF as part of its exit 
strategy. 
 
Issue # 3. 
 Relationship  and Partnership Between PwM, MDF and Afore Local Level  
 
 
Government Council (ALLG) 
 
This issue is very important because of the objection by the Afore LLG President to the CA submission. The 
forum was organized with the aim to discuss and address the issues raised by the President in his objection 
letter to the Minister for Environment & Conservation dated 18 March 2013. The conflict between PwM 
Executive Director and Afore LLG President started when the President was the Chairman of MDF 
 
Issue # 4.  
Support for Local Communities in the Proposed Managalas Conservation Area  
 
This is a very pressing issue as it allows communities/landowners to participate meaningfully in the project 
activities and especially the management of the Conservation Area  once it is declared by the government. A 
number of initiatives mostly economic alternatives were undertaken as part of the project to assist the local 
communities but most have failed due to number of reasons including management problems and high 
transport costs. This includes the marketing of okari nuts and the Managalas Organic Coffee Project (MOCP) 
to assist local coffee farmers to market their organically produced Arabica Coffee. The project did not put 
much emphasis on social development including health, education and support for women and youth 
although local community based organizations tried to carry out these programmes in their won cultural 
zones but most failed  for number of reasons including lack of community support, funding and capacity of 
the CBO management. 

6 
 
Issue #5.  
Major Economic or Resource Development Project Proposed for the Managalas 
 
 
Plateau 
While the work on having the Managalas Plateau declared a Conservation Area is being progressed there are 
other plans in terms of large scale resource development projects which is being pursued by other entities 
and groups. This will have a major impact on the area and will affect the plans for the area declared a 
Conservation Area. These resource development proposals include mineral exploration by Goldminex 
Resources, an Australian mining company and the plan for the Gora-Itokama FMA under the Oro Provincial 
Forest Management Plan. This will allow for logging in the area. Goldminex Exploration Licence number 
EL1547 expired in June 2013 but have been renewed after the Warden hearing at Afore in May of the same 
year. The Warden hearing was not attended by all clan elders in the exploration area. Only few individuals 
including the Afore LLG President gave the consent for the exploration to continue. EL154 covers villages in 
West Managalas including Anatua, Serefuna, Kokoro, Gorobuna, Kuai, Itokama, Naokanene, Umuate, Jaure, 
and Aiari and the main target for the exploration is the Sibium Ranges   which is well within the proposed 
Conservation Area. Another exploration work by Goldminex is in Zone 9  for which the exploration licence  
(EL1607) expired but was also renewed in 2013. Since the inception of the MCASP, the clans groups on the 
plateau through their clan elders have taken a strong stand againt any form of large scale resource 
development projects in the area. Therefore, this issue was selected for the clan elders to discuss and re-
affirm their earlier stance against any such large scale resource development projects in the area. 
4. 
DISCUSSIONS OF THE ISSUES 
4.1 Issue #1 
Simon Savaiko, a member of the PwM started off the discussions by emphasizing on the importance of 
conservation especially in protecting and conserving the Queen Alexandra Birdwing Butterfly (QABB) as 
shown in the picture below which is rare and only found in Oro Province with its main home now confirmed 
as being the Managalas plateau. 
Many participants raised concerns about the rumors that   the customary land will be taken by outsiders 
especially donors after the area is declared was one major issue raised and discussed at the forum. This is one 
reason, clan elders from certain parts of the plateau supported the objection to the Conservation Area 
submission by the Afore LLG President.  
Many participants raised concerns about the non completion of the boundary mapping project. They felt that 
they were not protected especially those at the outer boundaries who share land boundaries with outside 
clans. They want the mapping project to be completed for this purpose and also for purposes of the court 
actions against the government and mining company carrying out explorations in the area. 

7 
 
Some participants also stated that one of the main objective of the Conservation Area project is to protect the 
Queen Alexander Birdwin Butterfly (QABB), the flagship of Oro Province but now work has been done to on 
this. They suggested for a specific activity to be developed to set up  QABB ranches in each zones or villages 
including provision of training to the ranch keepers. 
 
Clan elders who attended the forum raised the issue of non-recognition of their roles and payment of 
allowances for their role in the project. They felt that they were well recognized for their role when the 
project  was initiated but this is not the case now. They want this to change so that they can be recognized for 
their roles. They may be forced to withdraw their support for the project if their needs are not properly 
address by both PwM and MDF. 
 
4.2  
Issue#2 
 
The Facilitators decided to give the opportunity to past and current staff members of MDF and board 
members to share their experiences with regard to the management and related problems faced by MDF and 
their working relationship with staff of PwM. It was emotional moment for some of them who shared they 
experience about using their limited education and knowledge to help bring MDF since its establishment to 
the current stage. They challenge new people who will take on the roles with the organization to put the 
people in their hearts and not for their own personal gains. They also emphasised the need a training needs 
assessment to be developed for MDF as well as capacity building strategy for staff and institutional capacity 
strengthening for MDF as an organization.Institutional strengthening of MDF is key to resolving the capacity 
gap and management problems with MDF. 
 
It was pointed out that currently MDF is down to only two staff members as the board has not recruited the 
new staff for the positions that are vacant. The MDF board clarified this point, saying that the positions were 
advertised and applications were received which it has screened but decided to withdraw the three 
management positions because there were no suitable candidates. These positions will be re-advertised for 
potential candidates to apply again. There are too many gaps in the current management structure in terms 
of capacity.   
A number of participants raised concerns about funding for MDF through the project and the ability for MDF 
to raise its own funding for its programmes. They were concerned that while the funding from Rainforest 
Foundation Norway is for this project which should be used to build capacity of MDF staff and strengthen the 
organization, instead most of the funds are used to cover administrative costs including staff costs for PwM. 
For this reason they said MDF should get its own funding for its programmes rather than relying on PwM for 
the funding. MDF is on the ground and knows the problems and issues well so it is bestter placed to address 
these issues that PwM, whose staff only fly in and out of the project area. Many participants said this type of 

8 
 
operations by PwM should stop and whoever is responsible for coordination of the project should should be 
based either in the project site or in Popondetta to work closely with MDF in implementing the project 
activities including capacity building of MDF staff..It was clarified that in order for MDF to raise its own 
funding it must have audited accounts and there must be capacity within the organization especially financial 
management. This was part of the exit strategy that was developed approved in 2009 but was never

INTRODUCTION 
Phase (I) of the Managalas Conservation Project will end after the area is declared a 
Conservation Area by the Governor General of PNG. That is after all the eight steps under the 
Conservation Areas Act 1978 are fulfilled. Phase (II) will mainly focus on the establishment of 
a Conservation Area Management Plan Committee (CAMPC), a Management Plan, a Ranger 
Program, and to strengthen and gradually transfer the responsibilities to the existing local 
NGO Managalas Development Foundation Inc (MDF).  In fact, PwM and MDF have already 
embarked on some of the activities in Phase (II). Draft of the Management Plan is in progress, 
establishment of the CA Committees in the communities or zones have been done and moving 
on to the establishment of the main Project CA Committee.  This year we have started on with 
awareness and initial collection of names to develop a Ranger Program. The zone mapping 
and land use mapping which is all part of the Management Plan are still far from complete.  
There are of course challenges that will be encountered in Phase (II).   
 
This report details the work done by the CBOs in establishing CA Committees in their 
respective zones and the combine meeting held at afore to appoint the four representatives 
that will represent the Landowners in the Conservation Area Management Plan Committee. 
There were also other agendas that were also talked about during the session of the meeting.  
PURPOSE 
The main purpose was to appoint the four representatives that will represent the Managalas 
communities in the Conservation Area Management Plan Committee. In addition, collect 
reports on the activities assigned to the CBO managers during the combine forum, and 
discussed with the committees on the development of the Ranger Program which will be part 
of the Management Plan but will be dealt with separately as it might cause confusion doing a 
lot of things simultaneously.   
 
Money and food for the Zone mapping in 7a and 7b was also given to CBO Managers and 
Kingsford to implement the activities. Reports by the CBO Managers and Kingsford Nichoi are 
attached.

METHODS/PROCEDURES 
We took off to Popondetta on the 25th November and overnight at Oro Guest House. Next day 
we did our shopping in town for the meeting, zone 7a and 7b zone mapping, and the 
monitoring and evaluation activity. We arrived at Afore at 6pm, some participants were 
already there.  
 
The meeting was held at the Afore Guest House. The first agenda of the meeting was a briefing 
again on the responsibilities of the CA committees. I went through with the participants,’ 
section of the  CA Act that outlined the responsibilities of the committee.   
 
We also touch on the agenda of the ranger program. In previous workshops we have collected 
names from individual clans to become rangers. However; the name list went up as far as 300. 
There were also other options given to appoint rangers zone base or LLG to reduce the 
number and also manageable provided the limited financial resources. First and foremost is to 
establish the CA committees which we have completed for the zones and now to the main 
committee which we have started with the appointment of the four representatives for the 
ten zones and dissemination of interest letters to some of the stakeholders. After this is the 
management plan which is in its draft form and this is to be drafted and finalised by the CA 
committee, and approved by the National Government. After all the above is complete we can 
concentrate in developing the Ranger Program, as the rangers will be implementing the 
management plan.   
    
The next agenda was the appointment of the four representatives to represent the 
landowners in the main CA committee. Participants were given time to lobby among 
themselves to appoint two reps each from the eastern and western plateau. After lengthy 
discussions amongst themselves they finally came up with four representatives shown in the 
result section below.  
         
Report and acquittals for the work of mobilising the communities to appoint zone CA 
committee members and chairman were collected and reimbursements were given to CBO 
managers as they were asked to use their own funds to carry out the activity. Their reports 
contain the names of the zone committee members that are inserted in the committee 
structure in the result section below. 
 
I met with the zone 7a and 7b managers and Kingsford Nichoi to plan the zones mapping and 
deliver the food rations and fund to use during the mapping. We Schedule the timeframe for 
the activity and the outcome that were expected from the mapping exercise. Kingsford was 
engaged because the two managers were still uncertain on the use of the GPS. Reports and 
acquittal for the money that they signed out from the Conservation Coordinator were 
submitted. The reports are attached in this report and zone mapping boundary GPS Points.

Another activity that was also arranged for zones 7a and 7b was the zone mapping exercise. 
Below is the completed map for these two zones.  
 
 
 
 
Reports on these activities from field officers are attached in this report. There are six more zones 
that will conduct their zone mapping next year 2013, and then will go on to mapping the land use 
types in each zone. Conducting the land use map at the zone level will be much easier then at the 
clan level. The main issue that will occur at the clan level will be land disputes which will slow the 
progress of the land use exercise. The clans have already sketch their land use plan but it was not 
done to scale.  Future plans would be to give them their sketch maps and collect GPS points for 
the main land uses that they have indicated in the sketch maps. The main land uses that will be 
featured in the land use plan in all zones will include; Conserved Areas, Agricultural Areas 
(gardening), Sacred Sites, Cultural Areas (Masalai Ples), and Settlements (villages). There will be buffer 
zones for the conserved areas which will be the hunting areas.  
 
The zone border lines do not divide the land for the various clans in the different zones but 
portray in general the location of the zones and the villages therein. Actually the villages shown 
in the map are the census units where the 2002 National Election was conducted. Population 
estimates for each zone can easily calculated using available data from the National Statistics 
Office. This can also guide where we can focus our awareness on family planning and other health 
issues.  
 
There were also some data collected in preparation for the development and implementation of the 
ranger program. Data include the number of clans in each zone, tribes and names of two rangers

ACTIVITY: Facilitator Training Workshop 
 
VENUE: Dareki, Zone 7A 
ATTACHMENTS: 1. Philemon Balasi’s letter 
 
INTRODUCTION 
 
The facilitator training workshop is the next major activity that follows after the Introduction workshop. 
This is the workshop where the actual clan group facilitators get to attend as topics of discussion in the 
flipcharts are dissected and discussed. The RFL and consensus building coordinators on the ground act as 
facilitators in this workshop. Given the number of participants at these workshops, it is divided into two 
separate workshops  one to cater for participants from the eastern zones (6‐10) and one for the western 
zones (1‐5).  
 
PURPOSE 
The  purpose  of  this  trip  was  to  oversee  the  proceedings  of  this  workshop  and  to  step  in  to  assist  in 
elaborating on issues that needed further insights. 
Furthermore, it was also an opportunity to attend the first meeting on the Managalas Day celebrations. My 
role there was purely as an observer to make note on proceedings and report back.  
 
DAY JOURNAL OF ACTIVITIES 
Friday 12 Aug 2011: 
Pom  Pop  
Leaving  on  the  mid  afternoon  PX  flight,  I  arrived  at  Popondetta  to  find  that  Chrispine  Burava,  Bradley 
Dabadaba and PWM officer Eddrick Ninimiro had not yet arrived so I checked in at Oro Guest House where 
Patrick and the two NARI consultants had also checked in after returning from Afore that same day. 
 
 

Activity Report   
 
 Facilitator Training Workshop 2011 
 
Consensus Building  
 
 
Dareki (zone 7A) 
./2 
Saturday 13 Aug 2011:  Pop ‐ Afore 
After doing all necessary shopping (having handed over the moneys of the workshop to Burava earlier) we 
took to the road at around 3pm arriving at Afore around 7pm. Dropping off the food and materials for the 
east workshop there, we continued on to reach Serefuna around 10pm where the rest of the cargo  those 
belonging to the west workshop were offloaded as we bid goodbye to Burava. 
Sunday 14  Monday 15 Aug 2011: 
Afore 
I found out from Dabadaba then that the date of the workshop had been moved back to Wednesday 17 of 
August 2011. So for the two days I had to stay at the guesthouse. 
Initial plans of having this meeting today did not eventuate as there was a death in Kauoki and villagers of 
Dareki had to attend the funeral there.  
Meanwhile, I am also awaiting the arrival of PWM officers John Niles and Ninimiro from Popondetta later 
this afternoon. I was later to discover on Monday afternoon that Niles met with a mishap and had to return 
to Port Moresby. 
Tuesday 16 Aug 2011:  Afore ‐ Dareki 
On the afternoon, after the arrival of Ninimiro we packed our bags and left Afore for Dareki, arriving there 
at  7pm  in  the  night.  We  had  to  leave  in  the  afternoon  because  the  heat  during  the  day  was  quite 
unbearable. 
Wednesday 17  Friday 19 Aug 2011: 
Dareki 
By the morning, it was apparent other participants who were still making their way to Dareki. As a result we 
had to wait until 10am to have the workshop started. 
A quick session on the Managalas Day followed on Thursday morning where Chiefs and community reps 
discussed on this important event. More on this topic is in the discussion section below. 
A breakup of the proceedings of the workshop looked like this: 
Day 1: Session 1  Flashback 
After initial introductions, this session was a throw back at previous topics that were  discussed in such 
workshops  with  a  review  of  previous  flipcharts.  According  to  participants,  issue  that  stirred  up  more 
discussions and questions included Climate Change, Disaster Risk Management and Land Use Planning.  
There were some hints raised by some that some of the issues discussed in previous RFL materials were 
only talk and actual actions were never taken by either villagers properly promoted by Zone supervisors, 
managers and activity coordinators. Peter Sokane (Zone 8) pointed out the village of Dareki as a classic 
example  of  people  not  taking  heed  of  advice  found  in  the  learning  material,  especially  with  regard  to 
solutions for Disaster Risk Management which explicitly states that houses near rivers should be moved a 
fair bit in onto higher ground. 
 

Activity Report   
 
 Facilitator Training Workshop 2011 
 
Consensus Building  
 
 
Dareki (zone 7A) 
./3 
Day 1: Session 2  Discussion on flipchart topics 
It was apparent from the onset that not everyone in the Eastern Zones know Barai  the language that the 
flipchart  was  translated  into.  This  is  especially  true  for  zones  9,  7A  and  8  and  as  such  will  be  a  major 
impediment in correctly getting this information out to the people.  
To address this problem, Kingsford Nichoi (MDF Conservation Officer), a Barai man stepped in to translate 
on the go. However, it became hard not miss the fact that this was taking its toll on the concentration level 
of the participants and draining their interests.  
It was then resolved that this session should be moved to the following day after Nichoi had everything 
translated. 
Day 1: Session 3  Qualities of being a good facilitator  
This session covered the little techniques and details in how to be a good facilitator so that the information 
was correctly transferred, digested and discussed. 
Day 2: Session 1  Managalas Day 
After I touched on the idea of the Managalas Day concept, pointing out my presence there solely as an 
observer, I left the floor to them to pick it up from there. From then on the discussions were taken up by 
the chiefs who were present then along with representatives from each of the Eastern zones who were 
present there.  
Day 2: Session 2  Discussion on flipchart topics: Take 2 
After Nichoi had everything translated and transferred on to butcher charts, they were hung up for the 
participants to manually correct and enter it into their copies of the flipcharts.  
Day 3: Session 1  Discussion on flipchart topics: Continuation 
Only one topic which was not covered yesterday was discussed on the third day. That was the topic of 
Climate Change. Here I also stepped in to break down the basics of this subject, laying it down for them in 
laymens term for their ease of comprehension. 
The workshop ended early Friday after the conclusion of the last topic of discussion. We then left for Afore 
in the afternoon of Friday when it was a lot more cooler.  
Saturday 20  Sunday 21 Aug 2011: 
Afore 
The whole of Saturday and Sunday was spent at Afore. During that time I discussed with Dabadaba and the 
theatre director, Alkin Fufus, with regard to their proposed fundraising walkathon venture from Managalas 
to the Central Province along the old Ghost Track. Details of this will follow below also.

FINDINGS & DISCUSSIONS 
 
Facilitator Training 
The workshop was held in Dareki. Given the dry spell currently experienced in the Managalas Plateau, this 
village is a suitable location of choice for this workshop because it is situated right next to the Pongani 
River.   
There were no major issues with logistics. Although it should be pointed out that we started a bit later than 
scheduled but still managed to cover everything within the scheduled 3 days.  
However,  there  were  problems  with  the  information  material.  Most  notable  of  which  was  the  delivery 
language of the information material. It was a bit late to note but the Barai dialect is not spoken by all the 
people of the Eastern zones.  
Furthermore,  as  pointed  out  in  the  introduction  workshop  at  Dea,  the  translation  had  spelling  and 
grammatical errors which further posed stumbling blocks for the information dissemination process. This 
issue needs to be sorted out and standardized so as to avoid such problems for future issues of Mama 
Graun Flip Charts. 
Managalas Day 
I covered the basics on the idea behind what Managalas Day (MD) was supposed to be all about. Stressing 
and ensuring that they all understood the fact that this was an event that they should take ownership of 
from the very beginning and that PWM was under no obligation to fund it in any way; that my presence 
there was simply as an observer to take note of proceedings in order to assist them in more of a supportive 
role by linking them with interested parties within our network and in helping to get the word out to the 
bigger public about this event. 
From then on several participants stood up to express their interest and excitement in having such an event 
to showcase the Managalas culture and the Conservation work to the outside world. 
A notable contribution was made by the Ward 3 Chief Mr David Womo of Kauoki village (Zone 7A). He was 
a former Provincial member in the Oro Provincial Government back in the Eighties and had widely travelled 
Papua New Guinea in his capacity as the Agriculture Minister in the Oro Provincial Assembly. According to 
him, he was also instrumental in the establishment of the Ese Highway from Pongani River upwards to 
Itokama back in 1983.  
With  such  a  background,  Chief  Womo  commands  much  respect  across  the  length  and  breadth  of  the 
Managalas Plateau. This was quite apparent from the reaction of the participants when he stood up to 
speak. 
He spoke mainly in their local dialect but it was obvious  and confirmed upon translation  that he was 
reiterating the importance of strengthening their culture, seeing Managalas Day as a key avenue in further 
promoting this to those outside as well as to the younger generation coming up. His speech was met with a 
loud applause from all those who were present. 
After he spoke, he was applauded by all present. His speech was followed by Mr Nevil Tieba, the chief of 
Numba village (Zone 6) and the Dareki Chief, Mr Jeffrey Dan. There were other community representatives 
present who also contributed, mostly re‐echoing the same sentiments.

Dareki (zone 7A) 
./5 
Here are some points that were captured during their discussion: 
1. David Womo:   Proposed to have MD moved to next year straight after elections. The key reason 
for this suggestion is mainly because of logistics.  
a. Yams have already been planted and there is not enough for this celebration. After harvest 
next year then they should have enough ready for this celebration. 
b. They need to prepare and fix their traditional attires in preparation for the celebrations and 
traditional festivities of this day. 
c. Awareness of this important activity has to reach ALL villages on the Managalas Plateau. 
This is so that all 18 LLG wards have to have their singsing group performing on that day.  
d. With these words he appealed to the participants at the workshop to deliver this message 
to all villagers to get ready for this great day. In his words, this will be the day when the 
rest of Oro and people from outside who are present will see what the Managalas Plateau 
is all about. 
2. Neville Tieba:   Supported the call to have MD moved to next year as a very reasonable suggestion. 
However,  given  the  current  dry  spell  being  faced  by  the  people  of  MP,  he  wants  to  have  the 
deferral of MD to next year as a tentative suggestion. If the current dry spell continues on to 2012 
to join with the forecasted draught of 2012 then they would be left with no choice but to defer it 
even further to 2013 even if it comes to that. He also reiterated the importance to have ALL villages 
on the MP to be a part of the celebrations of MD and to be involved even from the preparatory 
stages of this event. 
3. Jeffrey Dan: 
Supported both chiefs call and called on all facilitators to go back to their villagers 
and have all people check their gardens to have especially their yams and finery ready and in shape 
for the festivities of Managalas Day.  
Ghost Track and the Managalas Kuafienami Theatre Group 
The members of Managalas Kuafienami Theatre Group have proposed the idea of trekking the old Ghost 
Track as part of their fundraising drive in November of 2011. If all goes according to plan then they hope to 
embark on this exercise after the conclusion of the combine forum. 
This is an agenda that is not directly related to the consensus building process or any other PWM activity 
but since it was brought to my attention so I thought I should make a note of it here.  
Miscellanesous 
There was a request from Philemon Balasi of Zone 9 for a copy of the donors address book. They already 
have Berefo Community Development Association as an IPA registered association and have gone ahead in 
formulating a Community Strategy document back in 2009  a copy of which was given to PWM. 
As they want to seek other SLA‐style development options for their community, they have requested for 
these two documents or their copies at least. 
1. The donors address book 
2. Berefo Community Strategy 2009.  
According to him, several request have been made but there has been no success so far. Furthermore there 
is the request for their information to be made available on the internet. I have to first sight the mentioned 
strategic report. Refer to the attached letter from Mr Balasi. 

Activity Report   
 
 Facilitator Training Workshop 2011 
 
Consensus Building  
 
 
Dareki (zone 7A) 
./6 
RECOMMENDATIONS 
 
Facilitator Training 
To prevent future complications as witnessed here at the Facilitator Workshop as well as the Introduction 
Workshop, it is my recommendation that all future Mama Graun Flip Charts and other learning materials 
be written ONLY in Tok Pisin. 
From  then  on,  facilitators  can  read  in  Tok  Pisin  and  explain  in  their  local  vernacular.  Given  the  various 
strands  of  dialects  on  the  plateau,  Bara  or  Ese  is  just  not  sufficient  enough  for  the  exercise  of  the 
dissemination of information to the village people. 
Managalas Day 
Given PWMs role on this agenda, I am in no position to make recommendations. However, I just want to 
re‐echo the sentiments of the chiefs and the community reps at the meeting.  
I believe the deferral is a wise move and it will be beneficial for all parties involved so that nothing is left 
out  in  the  manner  of  necessary  logistical  requirements.  This  will  also  give  them  time  to  ensure  no  one 
misses out to be part of that day. 
As  a  first  of  its  kind,  this  is  planned  to  be  a  big  event  that  will  set  a  precedent  for  future  such  shows. 
Therefore this will have to also be an issue of discussion at the combine forum I suspect. 
Ghost Track and the Managalas Kuafienami Theatre Group 
Given my previous trekking exercise in the Hope Trek initiative, I want to be part of this exercise if possible. 
This will take place a week after close of the Combine forum so I should have ample time to recoup after 
the forum to join the MKTG in this venture. 
 
CONCLUSION 
 
The key finding is the problem with the translation on the Mama Graun Flip Charts. As mentioned from the 
onset, it was shoddy work and idea of translation should be done away with.  
Managalas Day has been moved back to be a major activity in 2012 right after the national polling period. 
Meanwhile, the Managalas Kuafienami Theatre Group is all set to trek the old Ghost Track in November 
2011, right after the combine forum. 
All in all, were on schedule and look forward to the combine forum in November. All photographs of Dareki 
are in its respective folder within the Managalas network folder. 
 
By Nichson I. Piakal

produced by Nancy Sullivan and Associates (NSA) and ensuring that the draft is edited
